title: Water heater thermistor fault
shortDescription: Bliss BB2000 / Discovery DLS thermistor reading invalid.
fullDescription: Bio Bidet's hybrid heating system uses a tank thermistor. E1 lights when readings exceed valid range. Power cycle clears spurious faults; persistent E1 needs warranty service.

faq.a: No - heater locks out for safety.

title: Tank refill timeout
shortDescription: Tank failed to fill within 90 seconds.
fullDescription: When the inlet solenoid opens but the float never reaches HIGH within 90 seconds, the controller logs E2. Inspect the angle stop and inlet filter.

fixSteps.title: Open valve
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm angle stop is fully open.

fixSteps.title: Clean inlet filter
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect supply hose, rinse the inlet screen.

title: Wand drive stalled
shortDescription: Encoder pulses missing during wand extend or retract.
fullDescription: The wand carriage is moved by a small motor with optical encoder. Scale on the wand sleeve increases drag and the encoder times out, raising E3.

title: Seat occupancy fault
shortDescription: Body sensor stuck in occupied or empty state.
fullDescription: Capacitive body sensor must transition from empty to occupied. E4 means the sensor is reading a constant value - typically because of moisture under the seat ring.

fixSteps.title: Dry pad
fixSteps.instruction: Lift the seat and dry the underside.

title: Heater overtemp lockout
fullDescription: If the tank exceeds 100C, a one-shot thermal cutoff opens. E5 indicates the cutoff has tripped - the tank assembly must be replaced.

title: Dryer fan blocked
fullDescription: E6 indicates the fan tach has dropped. Vacuum the rear intake grille to clear lint and dust.

fixSteps.title: Vacuum intake
fixSteps.instruction: Use a brush attachment to clear the rear grille.

title: Side panel ribbon disconnect
shortDescription: Side control panel ribbon cable seated incorrectly.
fullDescription: Bliss models have a side panel attached by a flat ribbon connector. After cleaning the panel can pop loose, raising E7.

fixSteps.title: Reseat ribbon
fixSteps.instruction: Snap the side panel back firmly until it clicks.

title: Supply T leak
fullDescription: Most Bio Bidet leaks come from over-tightening the brass T compression nut. Replace the rubber washer instead of cranking harder.

fixSteps.title: Replace washer
fixSteps.instruction: Shut water, swap washer, hand-tight plus quarter turn.

faq.a: Recommended; Bio Bidet ships one in the box.

title: GFCI tripped
fullDescription: All Bio Bidet seats need a GFCI outlet. After a brief surge or moisture event, the outlet may trip, killing the seat. Reset and check.

title: First wash is cold
shortDescription: Tank reservoir not yet up to temperature.
fullDescription: Bliss tanks heat the first 20 seconds of water and then run cool until refill. This is normal behavior, not a fault. Use Eco-Heat OFF for instant warm.

fixSteps.title: Disable Eco-Heat
fixSteps.instruction: Hold the ECO button until the LED turns off.
